title: A rerun after a migration already applied dies on an exit-5 alias collision, not an idempotent no-op
description:
Filed from LCLI-525 (opum-doc DEC-172 (4af), relay 571, 15:22:58Z). LCLI-525's hint was narrowed to arm A precisely BECAUSE a rerun is not a recovery — this records the underlying defect. DO NOT IMPLEMENT until opum-doc returns the shape choice (DEC-172 (4af)).

THE DEFECT. When a backlog's migration receipt already exists (same migrationDigest), a rerun of `lore init --tracker quest --migrate-backlog --remove-backlog` is neither a no-op nor a clean refusal: the migration re-engages and dies on the aliases the FIRST run created.

EVIDENCE (real double migration: temp git repo OUTSIDE the repo, backlog/ with 2 tasks, `quest init`, LORE_QUEST_ACTOR set so the migration can write; lore run from dev):
- RUN 1 (the reported case): type=denied, EXIT 4 — "refusing --remove-backlog: backlog/ has uncommitted changes, which git could not restore after a deletion". The migration APPLIED (3 Quest records created); backlog/ left on disk. Its input already carried migrationDigest "4cf4c153a050dc1579668275e9cf58650dcbfb3cc23dbc2a14de5e680a4b30a0" and migrationApplied true.
- RUN 2 (identical rerun, backlog/ still unrecoverable): type=CONFLICT, EXIT 5. message="Alias collision: \"backlog:<root>:active:task-1\" conflicts with \"backlog:<root>:active:task-1\". ..." stdout empty, stderr empty; Quest records unchanged (3); backlog/ untouched.
- RUN 3 (the SAME rerun after COMMITTING backlog/, so `git status --porcelain -- backlog` was empty): type=CONFLICT, EXIT 5, the SAME alias collision. So the collision is NOT about backlog/ being dirty — it is the migration meeting its own aliases, and it fires before the removal is ever reached.
- Separately: no removal-only path exists — `lore init --tracker quest --remove-backlog` without `--migrate-backlog` is type=usage.

OPUM-DOC'S DIRECTION (DEC-172 (4af), verbatim): "a rerun against a backlog whose migration receipt (same migrationDigest) already exists should be an IDEMPOTENT NO-OP that recognises the receipt, not an alias collision at exit 5. Whether it exits 0 with the existing receipt or refuses with a named 'already migrated' code is a shape choice, and comes back to me before implementation."

NOT STAMPED: no assignee; opum-doc decides dispatch — and this is explicitly gated on the shape choice coming back first.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A rerun that holds a pending migration record runs at most ONE read-only Quest preview to fingerprint the current source. If that fingerprint matches the recorded migrationDigest, it exits 0, returns the existing receipt plus `alreadyApplied: true`, and applies nothing.
The same rerun WITH --remove-backlog performs the verified archive, then verify, then remove.

If that read-only preview's fingerprint differs from the recorded migrationDigest, the rerun refuses with a named divergence code, applies nothing, and says the backlog diverged from the recorded migration.
A test runs the LCLI-525 sequence end to end: the refusal, then a rerun, then a verified removal.

plan: 1. Retain the pending migration record across a refused --remove-backlog (move clearPendingQuestMigration AFTER resolveScriptedBacklogRemoval), so a rerun can recognise the receipt.
2. Make a same-source rerun an IDEMPOTENT SUCCESS: return the existing receipt with an additive alreadyApplied: true, applying nothing.
3. Detect a CHANGED backlog (a different digest) and refuse with a named divergence code.
4. --remove-backlog on a resumed run does the verified archive -> verify -> remove; no separate removal-only entry point.
5. Fold in the LCLI-525 residual: the migrationApplied comment gains the stable-receipt-field-where-it-is-not-constant half.
6. Tests: the three paths plus the LCLI-525 refusal -> rerun -> verified-removal sequence. Gates; rounds.
implementationNotes:
SHAPE RULED by opum-doc, DEC-172 (4ah), relay 574 ack, 15:44:23Z. Recorded VERBATIM:
- A rerun whose source matches an existing migration receipt (same migrationDigest) is an IDEMPOTENT SUCCESS: exit 0, the existing receipt returned, plus an additive `alreadyApplied: true`. No re-preview, no re-apply, no alias collision.
- With --remove-backlog, that same rerun then does the verified archive -> verify -> remove. No separate removal-only entry point gets built.
- A DIFFERENT digest (the backlog changed after migration) is not idempotent. It refuses with a named code saying the backlog diverged from the recorded migration.
- Tests cover all three paths plus the LCLI-525 refusal-then-rerun sequence ending in a verified removal.
Scheduled on lore-clis NEXT allowlist ahead of other items. NOT to be implemented under LCLI-525; when this lands, LCLI-525s hint can name the real retry in a follow-up.

ACs AMENDED under DEC-172 (4aj), opum-doc ruling A, relayed 2026-10-11. ORIGINAL (a): "A rerun whose source matches an existing migration receipt (same migrationDigest) exits 0, returns the existing receipt plus `alreadyApplied: true`, and re-previews and re-applies nothing." ORIGINAL (c): "A rerun whose digest DIFFERS from the recorded migration refuses with a named code saying the backlog diverged from the recorded migration." ACs (b) and (d) stand unchanged. WHY, in opum-docs words: "My (4ah) AC (a) wording `re-previews nothing` was over-tight. The property that matters is that nothing is applied twice; a read-only preview is the only way Lore can tell same from different." IMPLEMENTATION, also from the ruling: move clearPendingQuestMigration (init.ts:563) to AFTER the removal is resolved, so a refused --remove-backlog keeps its pending record and the rerun takes the resume path (tracker-migration.ts:111-127) rather than the fresh-apply path; a test asserts the pending record survives the refusal; and the test for (a) asserts exactly ONE preview call and ZERO apply calls.
